title: Stitchback latency-cost runbook (proto)
content:
Summary:

This is a proto runbook describing the "stitchback" benchmarking approach and a lightweight set of measurements for latency vs cost across candidate serving knobs. Stitchback = combining small proactive context prefetches + short-lived local slot stitching to reduce cold-step token emission without increasing steady-state multiplexing pressure. The goal here is pragmatic: reproducible text tables and simple ASCII charts that product and eng can paste into a design PR.

Scope and constraints:
- Workloads: conversational assistants (turn-based), 1–6 turns, average user prompt 18 tokens, model outputs variable 30–400 tokens.
- Test harness: synthetic replay from trace sample (trace id set: sample-2029-03-conv-bursts) + steady QPS generator.
- Hardware baseline: 8xA100-80GB pool (isolated), single-tenant GPU worker per instance.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p99 generation latency (end-to-end), tokens/sec per GPU, $/M tokens approximated using reserved capacity amortized rate.

Test configurations (short names used in tables below):
- base: baseline runtime, no prefetch, kv-cache cold on session start.
- stitch-1: stitchback enabled, prefetch size 32 tokens, slot retention 3s, quant int8.
- stitch-2: stitchback enabled, prefetch 64 tokens, retention 6s, quant int8.
- prefetch-only: prefetch 64 but no slot stitch; fallback cost model unchanged.
- quant-hybrid: stitch-1 with mixed quant (int4 for feed-forward layers)

Quick numeric summary (single-worker, averaged over 30m run):

Config      | p50 ms | p90 ms | p99 ms | tok/sec/GPU | $/M tokens
------------|--------|--------|--------|-------------|------------
base        | 98     | 210    | 590    | 9.2         | $14.8      
stitch-1    | 112    | 185    | 420    | 11.6        | $12.6      
stitch-2    | 132    | 200    | 480    | 12.4        | $11.9      
prefetch-only| 105   | 230    | 630    | 10.8        | $13.9      
quant-hybrid| 120    | 190    | 450    | 15.6        | $9.4       

Notes on the table:
- p50 increased slightly for stitch configs because aggressive prefetch can add a small upfront latency on short replies; p90/p99 significantly improve because later tokens rarely see full cold KV misses.
- tok/sec/GPU increases due to fewer cache-miss recomputations and better kernel utilization during stitched segments.
- $/M tokens is back-of-envelope based on reserved pool cost (monthly amortized) + measured throughput. This is intended for relative comparisons, not billing-grade numbers.

ASCII micro-chart: p99 latency over configs (lower is better)

p99: | base  ▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉ 590ms
      | prefetch-only ▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉ 630ms
      | stitch-1 ▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉ 420ms
      | stitch-2 ▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉▉ 480ms
      | quant-hybrid ▉▉▉▉▉▉▉ 450ms

Micro-observations (from traces):
- Long-tail behavior: stitch-1 shows a cluster of p99 events associated with sessions where user immediately requests long completions (>350 tokens) — prefetch buffer exhausted and stitch transitions to full decode path. Those are visible as stepped latency bumps; consider adaptive prefetch scaling by predicted completion length.
- Small replies: for <80 token replies, base had slightly lower p50 than stitch-2; experiment with conditional prefetch (only when expected reply > 48 tokens).
- Quant-hybrid improved $/M significantly while keeping p99 lower than base — tradeoff appears favorable for bursty workloads where steady throughput dominates.

Experiment runner commands (prototype):
- Generate synthetic trace: 
  python tools/trace_replay/generate.py --source sample-2029-03-conv-bursts --scale 1.0 --out traces/stitchback/trace.json
- Run benchmark harness: 
  bin/bench_runner --trace traces/stitchback/trace.json --config configs/stitchback/stitch-1.yaml --duration 1800 --collect metrics/prometheus:9091
- Quick local perf capture (single query path): 
  ./tools/local_invoke.sh --model starling-13b-quant --prompt-file tests/prompts/smart-reply.txt --collect-kv=true

Checklist for next iteration (short-term):
- Add model-level sweep: test across 7B/13B/30B family with same stitch knobs.
- Run multi-tenant variant: small co-located multiplex client to measure slot contention effects.
- Add end-to-end real-user trace (anonymized) to validate microburst behavior.
- Replace $/M tokens with fully instrumented cost model from billing team (linked ticket: JIRA-PRODOPT-742).

Decision rubric (proto):
- If stitch-1 reduces p99 by >=25% and reduces $/M by >=10% vs base on representative enterprise traces -> advance to canary.
- If quant-hybrid reduces $/M by >=30% with <=10% p99 regression vs stitch-1 -> prioritize quant profiles for Dedicated tier.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Does slot stitching interact poorly with function-calling or tool invocation patterns? (need targeted test).
- Memory fragmentation: stitch retention windows could increase worker-side memory churn under high concurrency; add an allocator stress test.
- UX surface: should we expose "stitchback" as a boolean toggle in console or only as an auto-opt? Early intuition: auto-opt with manual override.

Appendix A — short raw trace excerpt (sanitized):
- session 0x1a2b3c: turns: [user: 12 tokens], model output lengths: [210, 34] -> stitch segments matched; p99 event at t=402ms (prefetch refill)
- session 0x1a3d7e: turns: [user: 6], model output: [28] -> stitch added 18ms overhead, but overall throughput gain across worker observed

Appendix B — pragmatic charts (copy/paste ready)
1) Latency vs throughput summary (CSV)
config,p50_ms,p90_ms,p99_ms,tok_per_sec_per_gpu,cost_per_m
base,98,210,590,9.2,14.8
stitch-1,112,185,420,11.6,12.6
stitch-2,132,200,480,12.4,11.9
prefetch-only,105,230,630,10.8,13.9
quant-hybrid,120,190,450,15.6,9.4

2) Short blurb for the console team: 
- Recommended default for bursty chat workloads: enable stitchback auto-opt with max-prefetch 64 and retention 4s; pair with quant-hybrid profile for steady-state cost savings.

If you pick this doc up: please run the long-model sweep (script in linked PR) and drop updated CSV into /traces/stitchback/results/ with timestamps. Mark this doc in Confluence as draft when more data available (CONFLUENCE-OPTIMIZE-3245).

---
Author notes (Elena): I kept the runbook intentionally lightweight so eng/product can iterate quickly in PRs. This is a working draft — expect refinement after cross-model sweep and billing cost model alignment.
